name: Convair 240/340/440 / C-131 Samaritan
summary: Postwar twin-engine airliner and a DC-3 successor, with radial engines and tricycle gear, still seen as cargo planes and in turboprop Convair 580 form.

wings: Low, straight wing with large, round nacelles
engines: Two large radial engines (Convair 580: turboprops) in round nacelles
fuselage: Round, airliner-style fuselage with small, evenly spaced oval windows
Rounded nose with a flat windshield
Tricycle landing gear (nosewheel, not a taildragger)

tellTales: Twin-radial or turboprop low-wing airliner with a nosewheel and level stance
Round fuselage with a long row of small oval windows
Tall rounded fin and low tailplane on a DC-3-sized airliner

confusedWith.howToTell: The DC-3 is a taildragger that sits tail-low on the ground; the Convair has a nosewheel, sits level and is a larger, more modern airframe.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
